text:
maria: Heads up — during a routine restore smoke test we hit repeated decrypt failures for snapshot-archive-prod-2026-03-20. Error: AccessDenied on KMS CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-def-ghi when backup-uploader-prod tried to decrypt. Suspect RBAC/grant pruning after yesterday's IAM cleanup. attaching error snippet below.

kevin: ugh. can you paste the exact error lines and which role attempted the decrypt?

maria: error from s3->restore workflow: 
```
2026-03-20T15:02:14Z ERROR restore failed: kms.Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/backup-uploader-prod/i-0abcd is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-def-ghi (status code: 400)
```
role in question: iam role backup-uploader-prod (service principal is EC2 assume-role used by upload agent).

jordan: @sre-oncall any recent RBAC sweeps that could have pruned KMS grants or attachments?

sre-oncall: We rolled the "backup-uploader-prod" permission set in IAM yesterday as part of least-privilege clean-up. The change removed a cross-account inline policy that previously allowed kms:Decrypt via a grant. I noted we were going to replace it with a proper KMS Grant, but that follow-up ticket was delayed.

maria: that aligns. It looks like the grant was deleted but the new grant wasn't created, so restores hit ACL denial. This is affecting restores only; reads of existing objects still fine because they were already decrypted before.

kevin: action items — we need a hotfix to get restores back, and a postmortem on process: 1) re-create short-lived KMS grant scoped to backup-uploader-prod 2) run restore smoke 3) revert RBAC change if needed 4) add audit alerts. Thoughts?

jordan: agree. For hotfix we can either reattach the old inline policy (fast) or create a KMS grant (recommended). Which has the faster path?

julia: reattaching IAM inline policy will restore quickly but reintroduces the anti-pattern we were removing. Creating a KMS Grant via the KMS API should be quick if we run it from a trusted admin-runner. I can create a grant with operations=["Decrypt","DecryptMultiRegion"] and granteePrincipal=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader-prod. TTL 24h to be safe.

maria: please do the grant approach. Also we need to verify audit logs to see if any other tenants or snapshots were affected. Run CloudTrail query for KMS Decrypt failures and s3 restore failures between 03/19 00:00 and now.

encops-bot: automated-scan: Found 6 recent KMS Decrypt AccessDenied events across prod region in last 24h. Listing resources: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-def-ghi, arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/xyz-123. See run id 20260320-encops-41 for details.

kevin: @julia go ahead and create the grant. post the grant id here. Also attach the exact aws cli command so we can reproduce as runbook.

julia: running now from admin-runner (us-west-2). command: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abc-def-ghi --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/backup-uploader-prod --operations Decrypt --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"service":"backup-uploader","snapshot":"true"} 
```
grantId: 3f2b6e2a-xxxx-4cfe-b7a9-0d5c12345abc

maria: grant created, thanks. Triggered a restore smoke on snapshot-archive-prod-2026-03-20 now.

sre-oncall: smoke restore started; monitoring logs.

encops-bot: smoke restore logs: 
```
15:20:02 restore start snapshot-archive-prod-2026-03-20
15:20:05 kms: Decrypt succeeded for requestId=xyz-0001
15:20:10 restore completed successfully
```

jordan: nice. Now let's capture timeline and root cause: RBAC sweep removed grant attachment without executing the planned KMS grant migration. Need to prevent future gaps.

kevin: follow-up items for postmortem (assignments):
- maria -> collect audit queries (CloudTrail + internal access logs) and list all affected snapshots (due EOD)
- julia -> write a one-click runbook to create scopped KMS grants for backup-uploader-prod and backup-uploader-stage; include TTL and constraint templates (due tomorrow)
- jordan -> add CI check that flags IAM changes that remove policies referenced in active KMS grants (propose webhook into PR flow) (due next week)
- sre-oncall -> add an alert: X failed kms:Decrypt AccessDenied events in 30m -> pager if > 2 (due today)

maria: also recommend we add an audit log correlation: when a grant is deleted, emit slack alert with the grant id and related snapshots. We can get that from CloudTrail event name DeleteGrant.

kevin: good. Also check key policy: ensure it doesn't rely only on inline policies that can be accidentally removed; favor grants or KMS key policy statements that enumerate roles.

julia: noted. I'll add key-policy hardening checklist to the runbook. Also suggest we add a daily query that surfaces "grants with no attached active principals" and email owners.

maria: one more thing — cross-check for any unintentionally uploaded cleartext artifacts during the window. I scanned uploads and didn't find plain text dumps, but we'll run another scan.

encops-bot: scan-complete: no cleartext artifacts detected in objects created between 2026-03-19T00:00Z and 2026-03-20T16:00Z.

kevin: thanks everyone. Good recovery. We'll schedule a short postmortem doc and link the mitigation PRs. Closing thread when postmortem link is posted. :thumbsup:
